question.text: Per the current NISM XVII workbook, which of the following statements about gold as an asset class is INCORRECT?

answer.text: Gold serves as a hedge against inflation
Gold provides regular income in the form of dividends
Gold is considered a safe-haven asset during economic uncertainty
Gold has high liquidity in the market

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM XVII workbook states that gold provides no periodic income; appreciation in price is the only source of return. The other options (inflation hedge, safe-haven asset, liquidity) are explicitly supported. The Trap: Already-issued SGBs offered 2.50% p.a. interest, but that is a feature of the bond instrument; SGB fresh issuance is discontinued from FY 2024-25 per the workbook. The statement about dividends from gold itself remains incorrect. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XVII tests gold-asset-class features in the broader retirement-asset-allocation context; SGB-specific features (discontinued issuance, 2.50% interest, 8-year tenor) are tested separately.
